name: Qatar
summary: A maroon field with a white band at the hoist, separated by a serrated edge of nine points. With a ratio of 11:28, it is the only national flag more than twice as long as it is tall.
origin: Like other Gulf states, Qatar historically used plain red flags; a white band was added in the 19th century, in line with an 1820 treaty with Britain that asked friendly Arab states to show white on their flags.

The red darkened to maroon, reportedly because natural dyes darkened in the sun, and the colour was standardised. The current flag, with nine serrations, was adopted on 9 July 1971, shortly before independence on 3 September.

colors.name: Maroon
colors.meaning: The blood shed in Qatar's wars; the colour is often said to come from red dye darkening in the sun.

symbols.name: Nine-point serration
symbols.description: A zigzag dividing line with nine white points.
symbols.meaning: Qatar as the ninth member of the 'reconciled emirates' of the Persian Gulf after the 1916 treaty with Britain.

history.label: Red and maroon flags of Qatar
history.note: Various designs, sometimes with the name 'Qatar' or diamonds.

facts: Its 11:28 ratio makes it the widest national flag.
Bahrain's flag is similar but red, with five serrations and a 3:5 ratio.
Qatar's National Day, 18 December, is marked by flags across the country.
clues: Maroon with a white hoist band and a zigzag edge of nine points.
The only national flag more than twice as wide as it is tall.
Its colour is said to come from red dye darkening in desert sun.
A nearby kingdom has a similar red flag with five points.
